reference.title: Barbell Lateral Lunge
reference.listing: Video (title and product number from the listing URL; the page itself could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you step out and sit back, exhale as you push back to the middle.
breathing.cadence: About 1.8 s out and down, short pause, about 1.4 s back

prescription.tempo: Controlled: about 1 s down, short pause, 1 s up
prescription.load: Start light; the side step challenges balance under the bar.
prescription.progression: Add 2.5 kg when every rep reaches full depth with the heels down.

cues.text: Bar on the upper traps just below the bony bump at the base of the neck, hands just outside the shoulders, elbows down, shoulder blades squeezed. Stand tall, feet hip width.
Take a wide step straight out to the right, toes pointing forward or slightly out; land softly and keep the bar level.
Sit the hips back over the right foot, right knee over the toes, left leg straight with both heels down; chest up under the bar.
Drive through the right heel to push back to the middle and step the feet together; breathe out as you push.
Stand tall, re-brace and switch sides (the player mirrors).

mistakes.fix: Keep both hands pulling the bar evenly into the back and the trunk square.

mistakes.mistake: Knee collapsing inward or past the toes
mistakes.fix: Sit the hips back and keep the knee over the second toe.

mistakes.mistake: Heel of the stepping foot lifting
mistakes.fix: Step a little shorter and sit back into the heel.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back and the chest up.

kinematics.peak: 79 cm between ankle centres (about one leg length, shorter than the 60%-of-height standard in Riemann 2013)
kinematics.norm: Standardised lateral step of 60% of body height tested (Riemann 2013); self-selected steps were similar
About 80-90 degrees; knee flexion was about 13% lower than in forward lunges (Riemann 2013)

kinematics.peak: Step out 0.6 s, 1.2 s down, 0.3 s pause, 0.85 s up, step in 0.65 s

sources.title: GymVisual, Barbell Lateral Lunge, video (movement reference only)
Riemann et al. 2013, biomechanical comparison of forward and lateral lunges at varying step lengths (J Sports Med Phys Fitness 53:130-138)
Escamilla et al. 2008, patellofemoral compressive force and stress during forward and side lunges with and without a stride (Clin Biomech 23:1026-1037)

cautions: Unrack the bar from a squat rack (J-hooks at about mid-chest height) and re-rack it after the set; set the safeties or use a spotter.
Keep the bar on the muscle of the upper back, never on the neck.
Groin or knee pain: shorten the step and reduce depth.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shorter step and less depth while learning.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Stepping-leg knee extensors control the sit and drive the push back. Knee and ankle impulses were greater in lateral than forward lunges (Riemann 2013).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Stepping-leg knee extensors control the sit and drive the push back. Knee and ankle impulses were greater in lateral than forward lunges (Riemann 2013).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Front-leg hip extensor; works hardest out of the bottom. Longer steps raised gluteus maximus activity more than knee-extensor activity (Song 2023).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Front-leg hip extensor; works hardest out of the bottom. Longer steps raised gluteus maximus activity more than knee-extensor activity (Song 2023).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Both sides work: the stepping leg controls the wide position, the straight leg is stretched along its inner thigh.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Both sides work: the stepping leg controls the wide position, the straight leg is stretched along its inner thigh.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension and co-contract around the front knee.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension and co-contract around the front knee.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Lateral lunges asked more of the ankle than forward lunges (Riemann 2013).
muscleNotes.calves_l: Lateral lunges asked more of the ankle than forward lunges (Riemann 2013).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk tall and the pelvis level.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk upright; a forward-inclined trunk raises their activity (PMC8136561).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk upright; a forward-inclined trunk raises their activity (PMC8136561).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: The muscle shelf the bar rests on.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: The muscle shelf the bar rests on.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Squeeze the shoulder blades together so the upper back forms a tight shelf.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Squeeze the shoulder blades together so the upper back forms a tight shelf.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Pull the bar down into the back and keep the upper back tight.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Pull the bar down into the back and keep the upper back tight.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the bar to hold it in place on the back.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the bar to hold it in place on the back.

phases.label: Stand tall, bar on the upper back

guides.label: Hips sit back over the foot
